issues.legal_issue: The phrase “special Indian law” in the statutory exclusion from agriculturist debt relief refers to a special law enacted by an Indian legislature.
material_facts: The bank sought repayment of debts from agriculturist partners, and the lower appellate court had directed that the debts be scaled down under the agriculturist relief legislation.
The bank relied on the provision excluding debts due to corporations formed under specified legislation, including a special Indian law.
The governing General Clauses Act defined “Indian law” as a law enacted by an Indian legislature.
issues.conclusion: The Banking Companies Act is a special Indian law, so the statutory exclusion can apply to the bank’s debts.
issues.legal_principle: The words of a statute that convey a clear and unambiguous meaning should not be given a different meaning merely because of their setting. The Court relied on section 3(27)(a) of the General Clauses Act, 1897, and rejected the contrary interpretation in Indian Bank, Alamuru v. Krishna Murthy, AIR 1983 Andhra Pradesh 347.

predicates.agriculturist_debt_relief_proceeding: A proceeding seeks to apply statutory debt relief to a debt owed by an agriculturist.
predicates.creditor_is_corporation_created_under_sp: The creditor is a corporation created under a special law enacted by a domestic legislature.

issues.definition: When a debt-relief proceeding concerns an agriculturist’s debt to a corporation created under special domestic legislation, the debt-relief scaling exclusion applies.

issues.legal_issue: A corporation created by or under a special Indian law falls within an exclusion covering a corporation formed in pursuance of such a law.
material_facts: The bank was constituted under legislation that provided for the constitution of corresponding new banks.
The respondents argued that the bank was created by or under the legislation, rather than formed in pursuance of it, and therefore fell outside the exclusion.
issues.conclusion: There is no relevant distinction between a corporation formed in pursuance of a special Indian law and one created by or under it; the exclusion covers both.
issues.legal_principle: The Court interpreted the statutory phrase according to legislative intent and held that it covers a corporation that is the creature of a special Indian law, whether formed in pursuance of, by, or under that law. It rejected the narrower interpretation in Indian Bank, Alamuru v. Krishna Murthy, AIR 1983 Andhra Pradesh 347.

predicates.statutory_corporation_exclusion_case: A proceeding requires deciding whether a corporation comes within a statutory exclusion for corporations formed in pursuance of specified laws.
predicates.corporation_created_by_or_under_special_: A special law created the corporation or provided the legal basis under which it was created.

issues.definition: In a proceeding about the corporation exclusion, a corporation created by or under a special law falls within the exclusion.

issues.legal_issue: An ordinance having the force of law can constitute the special law under which a corporation is created.
material_facts: The respondents argued that the bank had first been created under an ordinance and that the later legislation merely ratified its creation.

The Court stated that even assuming the bank was created under the ordinance, the ordinance was law, and also noted that the later legislation provided for the constitution of the bank with effect from the relevant commencement date.
issues.conclusion: The bank was created under special Indian law whether its creation was attributed to the ordinance or to the later legislation.
issues.legal_principle: An ordinance is as much a law as an enactment of a legislature. The Court also relied on the provisions governing the commencement of the Banking Companies Act and the constitution of the corresponding new banks, and referred to R.C. Cooper v. Union of India, AIR 1970 SC 564, and Life Insurance Corporation of India v. Kota Ramabrahmam, AIR 1977 SC 1704.

predicates.statutory_corporation_exclusion_case: A proceeding requires deciding whether a corporation comes within a statutory exclusion for corporations formed under specified laws.
predicates.corporation_created_under_ordinance_or_e: A corporation was created under an ordinance or legislative enactment.

issues.definition: In a proceeding about the corporation exclusion, a corporation created under an ordinance or enactment is treated as created under law.

issues.legal_issue: A factual contention raised for the first time on appeal cannot be accepted when it requires pleading and proof and the relevant facts are not established.
material_facts: Some advances to the firm predated the bank’s nationalisation, while another advance followed it.
The advances were made through a cash-credit account, from which advances would normally be repaid and fresh advances made.
The record did not establish the balance outstanding when the bank was nationalised or whether the earlier advances had been repaid and replaced by fresh advances.
The respondents had not pleaded the contention in the lower courts and raised it for the first time in argument before the Supreme Court.
issues.conclusion: The Court did not allow the respondents to rely on the contention that the earlier advances fell outside the statutory exclusion.
issues.legal_principle: A factual contention that requires pleading and proof cannot be raised for the first time in argument on appeal when the necessary facts are not established. The Court distinguished Life Insurance Corporation of India v. Kota Ramabrahmam, AIR 1977 SC 1704, where the loans had been made by insurers before the corporation was created.

rule.if: supreme_court_appeal and factual_contention_first_raised_on_appeal and contention_requires_pleading_and_proof and relevant_account_facts_unestablished

predicates.supreme_court_appeal: The matter is an appeal before the Supreme Court.
predicates.factual_contention_first_raised_on_appea: A party raises a factual contention for the first time on appeal.
predicates.contention_requires_pleading_and_proof: The contention depends on facts that must be pleaded and proved.
predicates.relevant_account_facts_unestablished: The record does not establish the relevant account balance or whether earlier advances were repaid and replaced.

issues.definition: In a Supreme Court appeal, a factual contention first raised on appeal is not entertained when it requires pleading and proof and the relevant account facts remain unestablished.

issues.legal_issue: The statutory exclusion for debts due to corporations created under special Indian law is not invalid merely because a related exclusion also refers to corporations created under foreign legislation.
material_facts: The respondents asked the Court to declare part of the exclusion invalid under the constitutional equality guarantee, relying on an earlier decision that treated it as favouring British corporations.
The Court held that “special Indian law” referred to law made by an Indian legislature, so the exclusion also applied to corporations created under domestic law.
The respondents had not raised the constitutional point in the courts below.
issues.conclusion: The Court rejected the constitutional challenge and held the Banking Companies Act valid for purposes of the exclusion.
issues.legal_principle: The Court held that the reasoning in Indian Bank, Alamuru v. Krishna Murthy, AIR 1983 Andhra Pradesh 347, did not establish unconstitutional discrimination once “special Indian law” was interpreted to include domestic legislation. The relevant constitutional provision was Article 14.

predicates.constitutional_challenge_to_corporation_: A party challenges a statutory exclusion for debts owed to certain corporations on equality grounds.
predicates.exclusion_covers_domestic_statutory_corp: The statutory exclusion, on its proper interpretation, also covers corporations created under domestic legislation.
predicates.asserted_foreign_favouritism_does_not_ap: The alleged preference for foreign-created corporations does not describe the exclusion as it applies to domestic corporations.

issues.definition: When an equality challenge rests on alleged foreign favouritism, but the exclusion also covers domestic statutory corporations and the alleged preference does not apply, the exclusion is not invalid on that ground.

issues.legal_issue: Debts owed by the agriculturist partners to the bank were not subject to statutory scaling down.
material_facts: The partners of the respondent firm were agriculturists, and the High Court had directed scaling down of the debt under the agriculturist relief legislation.
The creditor bank was a corporation created under special Indian law, and the Court held that the statutory exclusion applied to it.
The respondents’ contention concerning pre-nationalisation advances was raised for the first time before the Supreme Court and depended on account facts that had not been pleaded or proved.
issues.conclusion: The agriculturist relief legislation did not apply to the bank’s debts, and the bank was entitled to recover the amount decreed without scaling down.
issues.legal_principle: The Court applied section 4(e) of the Andhra Pradesh (Andhra Area) Agriculturists Relief Act, 1938, which excluded debts due to qualifying corporations, and section 13, which provided for scaling down qualifying debts. It held that the Banking Companies Act was a special Indian law and that a corporation created by or under such a law fell within the exclusion. It relied on section 3(27)(a) of the General Clauses Act, 1897, and referred to R.L. Arora v. State of Uttar Pradesh, [1964] 6 SCR 784, R.C. Cooper v. Union of India, AIR 1970 SC 564, and Life Insurance Corporation of India v. Kota Ramabrahmam, AIR 1977 SC 1704; it overruled the contrary interpretation in Indian Bank, Alamuru v. Krishna Murthy, AIR 1983 Andhra Pradesh 347.

predicates.agriculturist_debt_relief_appeal: An appeal concerns whether statutory debt relief applies to a debt owed by an agriculturist.
predicates.debt_owed_to_corporation_created_under_s: The agriculturist owes the debt to a corporation created under a special law enacted by a domestic legislature.
predicates.no_proved_basis_to_treat_debt_as_outside: The record contains no pleaded and proved facts establishing that the debt falls outside the corporation exclusion.

issues.definition: In an appeal about debt relief for an agriculturist, a debt owed to a corporation created under special domestic legislation is not scaled down when no pleaded and proved basis takes it outside the corporation exclusion.
